name: PermitPeek
subtitle: See app permission changes
description:
PermitPeek compares an app’s code signing entitlements against a baseline you acknowledge, so you can review changes after an update.

Choose an application with the system picker. PermitPeek reads its static signing information without running it. Rescan compares entitlement keys and values, the app version, and the signing team against your baseline.

Review added, removed, and changed declarations. Acknowledge changes to replace the baseline. Failed reads do not erase it. Copy a local report or remove a watched app without modifying its bundle.

Coverage is limited to the main executable. Embedded helpers, network traffic, TCC grants, and complete effective access remain unknown. An absent network entitlement does not prove an app cannot connect. PermitPeek does not give safety or malware verdicts.

Open the inbox with Shift Command P. Settings offer another shortcut and a menu bar fallback if registration fails.

Try Sample uses fictional CanvasKit and QuietNotes apps to show changed declarations and an unreadable signature. Sample watches are separate from your live watches.

Signing metadata and baselines stay on your Mac. There are no accounts or app network requests. PermitPeek does not read app documents, monitor traffic, or upload software inventories.

More Mac menu bar apps by Barframe at barframe.com
promotional_text: Watch the code signing entitlements of installed apps. See added, removed, and changed declarations after an update, and keep a baseline you control.
